title: Architectural approach for Futuristic Cyber Audio Visualizer
context: The system requires a high-performance pipeline to process real-time audio frequencies and map them to complex 3D visual elements. The primary challenge is maintaining a consistent 60fps frame rate while performing Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT) and rendering high-fidelity neon/glitch effects across both desktop and mobile devices.
decision: Implement a decoupled architecture using the Web Audio API for signal processing and Three.js (WebGL) for the visual rendering engine. Use the 'AnalyserNode' to extract frequency and amplitude data, which will be fed into a custom GLSL shader pipeline. This allows the heavy visual calculations (glitch effects, neon glows) to be offloaded to the GPU, while the Web Audio API handles the audio processing independently of the render loop.
alternativesConsidered: Canvas 2D API (Discarded: Insufficient performance for 3D-like geometry and complex shader-based effects)
Pure WebAssembly for FFT processing (Discarded: Web Audio API's AnalyserNode is sufficient for the current scope and provides better integration with the browser's audio stack)

positive: Scalable visual effects using GLSL shaders
Standardized audio processing via Web Audio API
negative: Increased complexity in synchronizing state between the audio analysis loop and the animation frame loop
Higher initial development overhead for shader programming
risks: Mobile browser performance bottlenecks on low-end devices
Browser-specific autoplay policies requiring explicit user interaction for microphone access
